newsitem.title: USA: Navistar truck decision disappoints Street.
newsitem.headline: Navistar truck decision disappoints Street.

text.p: Analysts who follow Navistar International Corp said Friday they were disappointed that the company discontinued its next-generation truck program because it was unable to resolve issues with the United Auto Workers.

"I think it's disappointing," said Richard Henderson of Pershing Division of Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette. "But because of the (potential for) significant reduction in labor, it would be a tough row to hoe for the UAW."
McDonald & Co analyst William Cooke said Navistar, through its next generation truck program, would have reduced employment at its Springfield, Ohio plant to 2,000 from 5,000.
Navistar said it remains committed to new product development.

Pershing's Henderson said the decision to abandon the next generation truck program will put new attention on how the company executes its truck strategy. "I think the Street is going to place (Navistar) management under close scrutiny," he noted.
